page.layout: One printed page: running head at top with page number at top right; below it a heading line with title and emblem number; then a woodcut illustration (engraving, described under notes); below the woodcut, a four-line verse with a large initial T; at the foot a large woodcut initial Q.

l.i: Vt perit optato littore mersa ratis?
Hac tu mente notes, cui fors aspirat amica,
Hac eadem ne te que Vehit Vnda ruat.

page.notes: The woodcut shows a ship wrecked at a harbour mouth, with a city and hills at left, a tall column with an arch at right, and waves. The first verse line begins with a large decorative initial T. The first line is partly garbled in the scan ("Viden' Ventis" reads as printed with Ꞓ-like forms for V/U and long s). Lines 1 and 3 and 4 show ligatures and the printed forms "Vela", "Vehit", "Vnda" as read with V for consonant u. The large letter at the foot is a decorative initial Q, possibly a catchword or signature mark; it is not clearly a word.
